questions.question: What is the clinical significance of a "low insertion of the cystic duct"?
choices: A. It increases the risk of cholelithiasis
B. It may lead to inadvertent common duct ligation during cholecystectomy
C. It is a precursor to cholangiocarcinoma
E. It is always associated with a duplicated gallbladder
questions.detail: If the duct inserts low, the surgeon may mistake the common duct for the cystic duct, leading to inadvertent ligation.

questions.question: An "aberrant right posterior duct" is a critical anatomical variant for which clinical scenario?
choices: B. Right hepatic lobe liver donors
C. Diagnosis of Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis
questions.detail: The aberrant duct must be identified because the recipient will require two separate biliary anastomoses.

questions.question: A "long common channel" (>15 mm) in pancreaticobiliary maljunction increases the risk of:
choices: B. Choledochal cysts and biliary cancer
questions.detail: The junction occurring outside the duodenal wall allows reflux of pancreatic juices into the biliary tree, promoting inflammation and malignancy.

questions.question: "Acute calculus cholecystitis" is most commonly caused by:
choices: B. An obstructing gallstone in the gallbladder neck or cystic duct
E. Ascending infection from the duodenum
questions.detail: Mechanical obstruction of the duct by a stone is the primary trigger for acute inflammation.

questions.question: Which of the following is a classic cause of an "echogenic gallbladder wall" with posterior acoustic shadowing?
questions.detail: These entities all create an echogenic interface at the gallbladder wall or fossa that may cast shadows.

questions.question: Adenomyomatosis is characterized on ultrasound by echogenic foci in the gallbladder wall that demonstrate:
questions.detail: These are caused by cholesterol crystals trapped in Rokitansky-Aschoff sinuses.

questions.question: How can a gallbladder polyp be distinguished from adherent sludge on ultrasound?
choices: B. Adherent sludge will not have vascular flow
D. Sludge has a comet tail artifact
E. They appear identical on all sequences
questions.detail: True polyps are vascularized outgrowths, whereas sludge is non-vascular.

questions.question: According to the provided risk factors, which gallbladder polyp is most suspicious for malignancy?
choices: A. A 5 mm pedunculated polyp in a 30-year-old
B. Multiple small polyps in a patient with hepatitis C
C. A solitary, sessile polyp >10 mm in a 65-year-old
E. A polyp with comet-tail artifact
questions.detail: Large size (>10mm), sessile morphology, and older age are high-risk features for malignancy.

questions.question: Diffuse gallbladder wall thickening (>3 mm) in a patient with cirrhosis is typically due to:
questions.detail: Low protein levels lead to fluid-overload/edematous states, causing diffuse thickening.

questions.question: Gallbladder varices are a secondary sign of:
questions.detail: These are collaterals formed to bypass increased portal pressures.

questions.question: Which Todani classification represents "Caroli disease"?
questions.detail: Type V involves only intrahepatic biliary dilation, which is characteristic of Caroli disease.

questions.question: A "choledochocele" is classified as which Todani type?
questions.detail: This is a dilation of the intraduodenal portion of the bile duct.

questions.question: The "central dot sign" on CT, representing a tiny portal vein branch bridging a dilated duct, is characteristic of:
questions.detail: This finding is highly suggestive of the saccular intrahepatic ductal dilation seen in Caroli disease.

questions.question: Pneumobilia (air in the biliary tree) is most commonly seen following:
questions.detail: These procedures allow air to enter the biliary system from the bowel.

questions.question: What is the "rule of thumb" for the upper limit of normal for a common bile duct (CBD) diameter in a 70-year-old?
questions.detail: The CBD should be ≤6 mm before age 60, and 1 mm larger per decade thereafter (6mm + 1mm for 70s = 7mm).

questions.question: Biliary cystadenoma is a benign cystic neoplasm that occurs predominantly in:
questions.detail: This is a classic demographic for this multiloculated cystic mass.

questions.question: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC) is most frequently associated with which other condition?
questions.detail: Approximately 70-80% of patients with PSC have underlying Inflammatory Bowel Disease, most commonly UC.

questions.question: Which malignancy can spread hematogenously to the gallbladder mucosa?
questions.detail: Melanoma is one of the few tumors known for hematogenous metastases to the gallbladder mucosa.
